subject: Logging & observability entitlements — renewal orchestration and negotiation plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Planning: Observability renewals and entitlements

Team —

Octavian Health's observability contracts (Datadog, Grafana Cloud, Sentry) are up for renewal in Q4. I pulled the current entitlements and attached a summary (current_entitlements_summary.csv). Main ask: we need a short, vendor-focused negotiation plan that reduces unit cost while preserving 90-day diagnostic retention for production incidents.

Please gather the following by EOD Monday:
- 90/95/99th percentile ingestion by source (hosts, containers, logs GB/day) — Marcus
- Current retention tiers in use and any paid add-ons (e.g., log archival, egress) — Sergio
- Any open credit/discount commitments from last renewal and marketplace SKUs — Jordan

Initial levers I want considered:
- Retention slicing: move dev/non-prod to 7/14d, keep prod 90d on critical logs
- Sampling and indexing rules to reduce ingested bytes
- Committed spend vs overage trade-off modeling (12 vs 24 month)
- Push vendors for retention credits / migration assistance

Also prep a short one-pager we can share with vendor reps that lays out our target: 20-30% gross cost reduction without impacting incident response. I’ll schedule a vendor triage call next week to get preliminary quotes.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Platform Finance (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: current_entitlements_summary.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planning: Observability renewals and entitlements

Neha —

Attached is a usage snapshot (usage_snapshot_20270801.xlsx). High level numbers:
- Average log ingest: 3.6 TB/day; 95th peak ~5.1 TB/day.
- Hosts (metered): 1,120 hosts (mix of prod and non-prod agents).
- Current retention mix: ~60% of log volume on 90d, 30% on 30d, 10% on 7d.
- Sentry: event volumes are steady; main cost driver is high-sample transaction tracing, not logs.

Preliminary cost levers I think will move the needle:
1) Move non-prod/off-hours pipelines to 7d cold storage or drop; estimate 18-22% drop in daily ingest.
2) Implement deterministic sampling for high-volume services (edge) to shave another 10-12%.
3) Push Datadog/Grafana for committed ingested-GB credits and egress bundling.

I can run a quick pilot this month to simulate retention slicing on a small subset (payments, search) if you want before asking vendors for formal quotes.

—Marcus
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: usage_snapshot_20270801.xlsx
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@datadog.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Datadog Contracts <contracts@datadog.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Datadog renewal proposal — preliminary numbers and retention addendum

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the heads up. We've pulled your account's telemetry and attached a preliminary renewal quote (Datadog_renewal_quote_2027Q3.xlsx) plus a retention addendum stub (Retention_Addendum_v1.pdf). High-level options:

A) 12-month commitment (baseline): 15% off list for a flat commit that covers current 95th ingest. Retention add-on for 90->180d archival priced separately.
B) 24-month commitment: 20% off list + one-time migration credit equaling ~2 weeks of ingest.
C) Flexible commit + overage band: lower upfront commit, capped overage at 1.4x list.

Specific to retention: we can offer a temporary ‘staging credit’ (one-time) for customers who agree to re-architect ingestion and transfer cold logs to object storage integrated with Datadog archival. Also willing to provide a 60-day free trial of our log-processor sampling rules engine to prove headroom.

Open items from our side: exact 95th ingest definition, egress expectations to third-party archives, and whether Grafana Cloud will act as an aggregator for any subset. If you’d like, we can book a 45-minute negotiation call with the renewals and technical account team next Tue/Wed.

Best,
Sanjay Patel
Enterprise Renewals, Datadog

Attachments: Datadog_renewal_quote_2027Q3.xlsx; Retention_Addendum_v1.pdf
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@grafanacloud.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@vendorco.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Grafana Cloud — pricing options & retention bundling

Neha / Marcus —

Appreciate the context. Attached is our pricing grid for Grafana Cloud logs (GrafanaCloud_pricing_grid.csv). A few notes:
- We can offer a logs-only bundle that routes application logs to Grafana and keeps infrastructure metrics in Datadog; this often reduces Datadog bill by ~12-18% depending on routing complexity.
- Marketplace customers get an extra 7% off if purchased via the public cloud marketplace (we can map to your AWS account).
- We support automated tiered retention (7/30/90) with transparent cold storage export; there is a small egress fee for exports to third-party object stores.

If you want to run a split-routing pilot (payments/search logs to Grafana; security logs remain in Datadog), we can set up a 30-day eval and provide migration assistance credits.

—Elena Ruiz
Strategic Accounts, Grafana Cloud

Attachments: GrafanaCloud_pricing_grid.csv
From: Priya Menon <priya@sentry.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-04T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Sentry retention add-on options

Hi Neha —

Quick note from Sentry: for most customers the cost driver is transaction sampling and event retention for high-volume services. We can offer:
- 30-day retention included in current plan; 90-day retention add-on priced at a per-million-event rate (see attached).
- A performance review that can reduce tracing volumes via adaptive sampling policies — we typically see 10-25% reductions without losing SLO signal.

I attached our retention add-on brief (Sentry_retention_addon_2027.pdf). Happy to join the vendor triage call and walk through what to sample and how to keep error rates observable.

Thanks,
Priya Menon
Partnerships, Sentry

Attachments: Sentry_retention_addon_2027.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@datadog.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@grafanacloud.com>, Priya Menon <priya@sentry.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-05T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Logging & observability entitlements — renewal orchestration and negotiation plan

Thanks everyone — good, practical options. Quick consolidation and asks before we lock calendar for the triage call: 

1) Neha -> Vendors: please prepare a firm 12-month and 24-month quote that includes: baseline commit, explicit overage cap, and a retention addendum showing per-GB archival pricing. For Datadog, note we are evaluating split-routing to Grafana for non-security logs.
2) Vendors -> please include any one-time migration / staging credits in your quote (we want to convert those into negotiation currency).
3) Internal -> Marcus: start the 30-day pilot for payments + search logs to test 30d->7d non-prod retention and sampling rules. Run it on a subset flagged in the usage snapshot and report delta in ingest.
4) Jordan: can you confirm procurement runway (we expect to re-commit or sign a new merchant PO by 2027-10-15) and whether finance is ok with a rolling 24-month commit if the discounting meets 18%+ threshold?

I've created a short negotiation brief in Drive and added HubSpot record 67890 to the triage ticket. DocuSign preview link is included in case we get immediate buy-in from any vendor.

Proposed next step: vendor triage call Tue 2027-08-10 10:00 PT. If all vendors can provide the requested 12/24mo quotes by EOD Mon 2027-08-09, we'll take that call.
